title: X-ray Attenuation Calculator for Multicomponent Materials
description:
A graphical and programmable calculator, used in a web browser or installed locally, for narrow-beam X-ray attenuation in multicomponent materials and planar multilayers: glasses, ceramics, composites and filters.

From chemical composition (mass, mole or volume fractions) and density, it computes energy-dependent mass and linear attenuation coefficients, transmission and removed fraction, photoelectric, coherent and incoherent contributions, half- and tenth-value layers, attenuation lengths and the thickness needed for a target transmission, over 1–800 keV with sampling around absorption edges. It also evaluates user-supplied photon spectra and propagates density and thickness uncertainty by Monte Carlo.

Cross-sections are the Elam, Ravel & Sieber (2002) data via XrayDB; please cite that work as well.

Version 1.1.0 adds a browser version, at https://faizalusama.github.io/X-ray_attenuation_calculator/, that runs the same engine with nothing to install. Calculated numbers are unchanged from 1.0.0. The 0.1.x versions applied each mass fraction twice, so their multicomponent results understate attenuation; they are superseded.
